name_reason: Compliant: data_fd2_ prefix (game global data), ui domain (tactical-overview UI helper), descriptor reflects purpose (tactical overview screen, per-team marker colors) and data shape (table). No Ghidra address residue. The '2' in tactical-overview team ids (0..2) are semantic team ids, not address residue; the name carries no hex suffix.
purpose: Per-team marker palette color bases for the tactical-overview (zoom-out battlefield map) screen; indexed by a character's team id to tint that char's square.
logic_summary: 3 x int32 const table { 0x20, 0x50, 0x48 }. Sole reader fd2_open_tactical_overview_zoom (@ 0x2000a) copies all three dwords into a local team_color_table_a[3] stack buffer (3 x MOVSD from 0x5208A), then per visible character indexes it by the runtime_char team field (rt_char+6, values 0..2, stride 4 as a full dword) and adds anim_phase (0..7) to produce the palette index passed to fd2_fill_screen_rect_with_byte for the team-tinted marker square.
element_semantics: Indexed by runtime_char team id (rt_char+6 == struct field 0x0E 陣營). [0] 0x20 = team 0 (enemy/敵); [1] 0x50 = team 1 (ally / NPC / 友); [2] 0x48 = team 2 (player / 己方). Each element is a DOS palette color base; reader adds anim_phase 0..7 before drawing.
comment_original_issue: src comment labelled the three elements as 'player / enemy / neutral team', which is the wrong order. Per runtime_char struct team field (0x0E: 00=enemy, 01=ally/NPC, 02=player) and the index->team mapping, the correct order is enemy / ally(NPC) / player. The Ghidra PRE plate already had it correct.
notes: Read-only confirmed: only READ/DATA xrefs from the single reader, no writer. Ghidra datatype is int[3]/12 bytes (memory {32,80,72} = {0x20,0x50,0x48}); bytes beyond offset 12 in a 32-byte read belong to the next data item, not this table. Ghidra plate for this symbol lives in PRE_COMMENT (consistent with the whole .object2 UI table family, all of which use PRE not PLATE) and its content already matches the refined understanding, so it was left untouched.
